_meta.note: A pool of possible carriers, NOT a fixed cast. At the start of each game a subset is drawn from the seeded RNG, each is dealt an archetype, an entry turn and a personality, and only those enter. Two games from different seeds should not feel like the same opponents doing the same things.
_meta.determinism: The draw happens once in newGame and is stored in GameState.rivalPlan, so it rides along in the save file and the same seed always produces the same cast.
_meta.colors: One flat accent per carrier, chosen to stay legible on the paper map and to avoid the player's navy.

draw._comment_rivals: How many of the roster enter in a given game. Fewer means a sparser, easier world; more means a crowded one.
draw._comment_entry: The first rival arrives around firstEntryTurn and the rest follow at seeded gaps, so the difficulty curve differs run to run.
draw._comment_attention: Trailing-year player profit that pulls a rival in ahead of schedule. Pillar 4: success attracts sharks.
draw._comment_aggression: Personality roll. Scales how readily a carrier contests a market and how thin a profit it will accept. Two ULCCs in different games should not play identically.
draw._comment_thrift: Personality roll on cash discipline: how much buffer it keeps before expanding, and how late it retreats.
draw._comment_playerFocus: How much more attractive a market looks to a rival when it is the PLAYER flying it. Pillar 4 says competitors enter in response to visible player profits, so this is the design, not a thumb on the scale — the player is the newsworthy operator. At 1.0 rivals mostly end up raiding each other and the player never feels hunted.
draw._comment_reach: Personality roll on how far it is willing to fly.
draw._comment_gaugeBiasSpread: How far a carrier's fleet planning can miss the right-sized aircraft for a route. Each carrier rolls a gauge bias in [1-this, 1+this]: a sharp operator lands near 1 and flies the aircraft that fits, a poor one sits near the edges and chronically over- or under-gauges — too big and it flies half-empty, too small and it spills traffic to rivals. This is what stops every AI converging on the same optimal aircraft: some are simply better at fleet planning than others. 0 makes them all sharp.
